# UI dev + QA loop

Design skills (ui-ux-pro-max and similar) help you choose styles, palettes, and
patterns. They cannot check what you actually rendered. Most amateur-looking UI
comes from small execution errors: a 2px gap where there should be 8, two
buttons touching, a label cut off. Models miss these because they write CSS
without seeing the result, and because judging your own work tends toward
approval. This skill replaces judgment with measurement, then adds real
screenshots and an independent review.

## Definition of done

A UI task is done only when all of these are true. Report each one in your final message.

1. `npm run qa:ui` exits 0 on every configured state and viewport (or each remaining issue is allowlisted with a written reason).
2. You viewed the screenshots in `qa-out/` yourself, including the component crops.
3. New or changed screens have states added to the QA config (see step 2).
4. The project's own checks pass (build, type check such as `svelte-check`, tests).
5. For anything larger than a one-component tweak, an independent review ran (step 6).

If you cannot view images (your model has no vision), stop and tell the user. Do not substitute guesses about how the page looks.

## One-time setup per project

Do this only if `tests/qa/qa-ui.mjs` does not already exist.

1. Copy `scripts/qa-ui.mjs` and `scripts/qa-ui.config.example.json` from this skill into the repo as `tests/qa/qa-ui.mjs` and `tests/qa/qa-ui.config.json`. Committing them makes the gate permanent and independent of this skill.
2. Install dev dependencies where the frontend lives: `playwright` and, recommended, `@axe-core/playwright`. Run `npx playwright install chromium`.
3. Add a package script: `"qa:ui": "node tests/qa/qa-ui.mjs"`.
4. Edit the config: base URL, `startCommand` (the script boots the app itself and stops the whole process tree afterward, on Windows too), the app's states, and component selectors to crop. Add a `data-qa` attribute to key components rather than relying on fragile selectors.
5. For each state, set `ready` to a selector that only exists once the screen has rendered its data. The script never waits for network idle, because that never settles on apps that poll.
6. Make sure the app can boot with seeded data covering every state (empty, populated, long content, every status). If fixtures do not exist, create them. A gate that only sees the happy path catches little.
7. Make sure design tokens exist (next section).
8. If the app must meet WCAG reflow (SC 1.4.10), add a 320px-wide viewport to the config. The defaults are desktop sizes.

## 1. Build from tokens, not raw values

Consistency is the cheapest quality win, and it is enforceable.

- Find the project's tokens: spacing scale, type scale, colors, radii, shadows. If a design system was generated by ui-ux-pro-max, use it. If it was never saved to a file in the repo, save it first (CSS variables or the framework's theme file) so later work stays consistent.
- If no tokens exist, create them: spacing on a 4px base (4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48), a short type scale, a small semantic color set.
- Use only tokens in components. No raw pixel or hex values for spacing, color, or radius. Reuse existing components before writing new ones; if the project uses a kit (shadcn-style), compose from it.
- Interactive controls in one row share height, radius, and gap. Use layout primitives (flex/grid with `gap`) instead of margins on individual children, because gaps cannot go missing.
- Every interactive element gets a visible `:focus-visible` style, plus hover, active, and disabled styles.

## 2. Make the check fail first

When fixing a defect, reproduce it as a failing check before changing code: add or extend a state in the QA config that exposes it, run `npm run qa:ui`, and confirm the report flags it. Fix, rerun, confirm it passes. When building something new, add its states to the config as you build: empty, loading, error, long content (very long title and filename), many items, each status, and any open modal or menu. Add `actions` to the state to open the thing.

If the script cannot detect the defect (a hierarchy or balance problem), say so and rely on steps 4 and 6 for it. Do not weaken or skip a check to get a green run. If a check is wrong for a specific element, add a narrow allowlist entry with a reason.

## 3. Run the gate and iterate

```
npm run qa:ui
```

Read `qa-out/report.md`. Fix every ERROR. Treat warnings as a to-do list: target-size and off-scale spacing warnings are often real. Rerun until it exits 0. If the same issue survives three attempts, stop and report it with what you tried rather than looping.

What the script checks, at three viewports (1920x1080, 1366x768, 1024x768 by default):

- Layout: page and element overflow, off-screen content, clipped text, touching or overlapping controls, broken or distorted images, spacing off the scale.
- WCAG 2.2: target size (2.5.8), focus visible via a keyboard Tab walk (2.4.7, first viewport only), accessible names on icon-only controls (4.1.2), labels on form fields (1.3.1 / 3.3.2), plus axe-core rules when installed.
- Runtime: console errors, page errors, failed requests.

## 4. Look at the real pixels

The report cannot judge hierarchy, balance, or polish. After the script passes, open the screenshots in `qa-out/`. Prefer the component crops (`<state>__<viewport>__<component>.png`, captured at 2x), because full-page images are downscaled and hide 1 to 4 pixel problems. For each screen, check `references/common-defects.md` and look specifically for: uneven padding between similar items, misaligned icons and text, mixed button sizes, and anything touching an edge.

Describe concretely what you see ("8px gap between Save and Accept, both 36px tall"). If you cannot give a concrete description, you are not actually seeing the image; stop and say so.

## 5. Read your own diff

Before finishing, scan the diff for: raw px/hex values, missing hover/focus/disabled styles, an icon-only button without `aria-label` and a tooltip, text that can overflow with long input, and any state you did not add to the QA config.

## 6. Independent review (for anything beyond a small tweak)

Start a fresh session or subagent that did not build the screens, ideally on a different vision-capable model, and give it only the screenshots plus `references/review-rubric.md`. It lists defects with locations and severities; it does not approve or reject. Fix every P0 and P1, rerun the gate, regenerate screenshots, and re-review the screens that changed. If no second session is available, tell the user the review step was skipped.

## Autopilot mode (hands-off)

When the user wants a fully hands-off round ("run a UI round", "autopilot", or the `/ui-round`
prompt), follow `references/autopilot.md` end to end instead of stopping for triage. It defines
the triage policy, fix loop, stop conditions, and final report, so you never need to ask the
user anything. Supporting scripts: `scripts/canary.mjs` (reviewer calibration),
`scripts/review-manifest.mjs` (screenshot batching), `scripts/gate-guard.mjs` (stops the gate
from being weakened).

## Standards and limits

- The script follows WCAG 2.2 Level AA where it can be automated. Target size uses the real SC 2.5.8 rule: 24x24 CSS px, or the spacing exception (a 24px circle around the target touches no other target); inline links and native checkboxes/radios are exempt.
- Page loading follows Playwright guidance: `load` plus explicit `ready` selectors instead of `networkidle`, locator-based actions, reduced motion, and disabled animations in screenshots.
- The 4px spacing scale and the 4px `minGap` are project conventions and heuristics, not WCAG requirements. Tune them in the config.
- This is a gate, not a conformance audit. Automated checks cover only a subset of accessibility and visual defects. Keyboard-only use, screen readers, zoom, and text-spacing overrides still need manual passes if conformance matters.

## Final message format

Keep it short and factual:

- States and viewports checked, and the final `qa:ui` result
- Defects found and fixed (grouped), anything allowlisted and why
- Defects found but not fixed, with a reason
- Whether the independent review ran
- Anything you could not verify (for example, no vision, or a state with no fixture)

## Files in this skill

- `scripts/qa-ui.mjs` — the gate; copy it into the repo (setup step 1)
- `scripts/qa-ui.config.example.json` — starting config
- `references/common-defects.md` — the checklist of small defects to look for
- `references/review-rubric.md` — instructions for the independent reviewer
- `references/autopilot.md` — the hands-off loop, triage policy, and stop conditions
- `scripts/canary.mjs`, `canary/canary.html` — plants six known defects to test a reviewer model
- `scripts/review-manifest.mjs` — builds capped screenshot batches for the reviewer
- `scripts/gate-guard.mjs` — fails if thresholds, states, or the gate script were weakened
